claim: Sanskrit title is Arya-vajrapani-abhiseka-mahatantra
evidence: Search results catalogue Āryavajrapāṇyabhiṣekamahātantra = Phags pa lag na rdo rje dbang bskur ba'i rgyud chen po, Toh 496 (Vajrapani Empowerment Tantra); Komai's Vajrapāṇyabhiṣekatantra papers use same title.

claim: Sanskrit transliteration 'Sarvapata Natha Sharana Artha Dhishthah' in the text
evidence: No source found for this Sanskrit verse; it is a transliteration of a Tibetan-script rendering, not a checkable fact.

claim: The following is a transliteration of the Sanskrit mantra
The Jetsun telling the story of his life refers to the origin of the famous Biography of Milarepa
evidence: Sources state Milarepa told his life story at Nyanang (Belly Cave) at Rechungpa's request, which is the basis of the biographical tradition (Tsangnyön Heruka's Life, 1452-1507, drew on older biographies).

claim: Enjoyment Body = Sanskrit sambhogakaya
Essence Body = Sanskrit svabhavikakaya
evidence: Svabhavikakaya (ngo bo nyid kyi sku) means essential body, a fourth body in Vajrayana.

claim: Mishta is likely a transliteration of a Sanskrit term related to bliss or mixture
evidence: Could not find any source for Mishta in this Dzogchen context; possibly Skt. misra (mixed) or mistha (sweet) but no citation.

claim: Sanskrit mantra transliterated in Tibetan
Tibetan 'Rab kyi rtsal gyis rnam par gnon pa' = Sanskrit Vikrantagamin (Excellence of Power)
evidence: Vikrantagamin appears in sources as Tib. rnam par gnon pa'i gshegs pa (a buddha of the 35), not matching 'rab kyi rtsal gyis rnam par gnon pa'; the equivalence could not be confirmed and looks doubtful.

claim: Padmasambhava was invited to Tibet by King Songtsen Gampo
evidence: Padmasambhava was invited by King Trisong Detsen (8th c.), two generations after Songtsen Gampo.
correction: Invited by King Trisong Detsen, not Songtsen Gampo.

claim: Rechung Dorje Drakpa, 1084-1161, principal student of Milarepa
evidence: Rechung Dorje Drakpa (1083/4-1161), one of the two most important students of Milarepa.

claim: Physical description of a pothi folio
Sanskrit dharani for summoning Indra/Shakra
evidence: Merely restates the passage's own statement that these are the words for summoning Shakra.

claim: Sanskrit title Buddhavatamsaka-nama-mahavaipulya-sutra for Great Vaipulya Sutra of the Buddha's Ornament
Kama = Transmitted Precepts and Terma = Treasures; here the 'Jewel Ocean' (nor bu rgya mtsho)
evidence: Pema Lingpa extracted Lama Norbu Gyatso (Jewel Ocean) from a lion-faced rock at Mendo cliff in Lhodrak; terma = treasure, bka' ma = transmitted precepts is standard.

claim: Repa descended from Lapchi; benefactor Dormo offered welcome drink; teacher Shakya Guna requested teaching; song titled Song of the Six Essential Points
evidence: Shakya Guna is a real monk-teacher associated with Milarepa songs, but I found no source confirming the Lapchi/Dormo welcome episode or the exact song title; the note largely paraphrases the passage.

claim: Madhyamaka that speaks of external objects as existing = Sanskrit Sautrantika-Madhyamaka
evidence: Sautrantika-Madhyamaka (mdo sde spyod pa'i dbu ma) conventionally asserts external phenomena exist; contrasted with Yogacara-Madhyamaka.

claim: Sanskrit dharani/mantra transliterated into Tibetan
Tibetan Shā ra dwa ti'i bu = Sharadvatiputra, better known as Sariputra
evidence: 84000 lists sha ra dwa ti'i bu as a Tibetan form of śāradvatīputra, a contracted form of Śāriputra.

claim: Me-skyes (Fire-born) refers to Jivaka Kumarabhritya
evidence: Jivaka's Tibetan name is 'tsho byed; 'fire born' turns up in sources as the epithet of Jyotiska, a different figure, so the note's equivalence is doubtful and unconfirmed.

claim: Bimbisara = gZugs-can sNying-po, King of Magadha
evidence: Bimbisara was king of Magadha; Tibetan gzugs can snying po is the standard rendering.

claim: This is the final aspiration
Five crimes of immediate retribution: killing father, mother, an Arhat; wounding a Buddha; causing schism
evidence: The five are murder of mother, father, an arhat, drawing the blood of a buddha, and causing a schism in the sangha.
